claims.text: The feedstock is a FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy with a 15–45 μm particle-size distribution.
The feedstock is currently used for HVAF-i7 deposition on confined components with internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
Baseline HVAF-i7 deposition with 15–45 μm feedstock produces acceptable coating quality.
Baseline HVAF-i7 deposition produces inadequate coating thickness.
Increasing the HVAF-i7 spray distance to 300–350 mm will enhance in-flight particle acceleration.
Enhanced particle acceleration will increase impact momentum and kinetic energy.
Higher impact momentum will improve splat deformation and flattening.
Improved splat deformation will strengthen inter-splat bonding and adhesion.
Extending the spray distance gives particles more time to accelerate within the jet.
An inert deposition atmosphere will limit as-sprayed oxidation.
The increased spray distance will improve deposition efficiency.
Improved deposition efficiency will produce a significantly thicker coating than the baseline process.
The thicker coating produced at 300–350 mm will remain adherent.
The coating produced at 300–350 mm will retain low levels of as-sprayed oxidation.
The coating produced at 300–350 mm will withstand high-temperature thermal-barrier service.
The intervention will remain effective on components with internal diameters down to 120 mm.
The intervention's effectiveness depends on maintaining gas flow and feed rate near their baseline values.

contradictions.description: A 300–350 mm nozzle-to-substrate distance appears geometrically incompatible with deposition inside a 120 mm internal diameter if the nozzle is oriented radially; no alternative torch orientation or geometry is specified to reconcile these requirements.
